# [CS004] Server-Side Request Forgery (ssrf)

An outbound request is sent to a URL controlled by the client.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

The server's network position is trusted by internal services and cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254). A URL from the request lets an attacker reach them through the server. Requests whose URL is built from a fixed host are reported with lower severity; a URL taken entirely from input is reported as the taint flow.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func preview(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	resp, err := http.Get(r.URL.Query().Get("url"))
	if err == nil {
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		_, _ = io.Copy(w, resp.Body)
	}
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func preview(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	u, err := url.Parse(r.URL.Query().Get("url"))
	if err != nil || u.Scheme != "https" || !allowedHosts[u.Hostname()] {
		http.Error(w, "host not allowed", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	resp, err := client.Get(u.String())
	if err == nil {
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		_, _ = io.Copy(w, resp.Body)
	}
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [ssrf]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    ssrf: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore ssrf -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** ssrf
```
